messages:
omar: Heads-up — nightly-perf job flagged a regression in kernel routing vs. the replay harness. p95 latency up ~18% on seq=1024 workloads. CI alerted at 03:10 UTC.

jess: ugh. which kernel selector change landed in the last release?

matt: looks like PR #4128 (adaptive-kernel-priority) rolled yesterday. I added a logging flag but didn't expect this diff.

omar: attach: perf summary from the job (abridged). replay harness: p95=118ms, baseline=100ms. synth-loadgen (same shape): p95=102ms. KV cache hit-rate for replay run is 62%, synth is 87%.

rachael: that KV hit-rate difference is suspicious — replay includes longer-tail prefixes, so warmup matters. Did the replay runner run the prewarm stage?

infra-bot: nightly-perf job #7285 started (replay-runner)

matt: double-checked: replay-runner used `--prewarm 0` due to an earlier change. The synth job uses `--prewarm 1000`. so replay wasn't warming KV.

omar: that explains part of it, but the kernel selector still chose a different kernel under the same model shape when the cache was cold. Need apples-to-apples: both runs must use same prewarm and same seed.

jess: agreed. propose: 1) rerun replay with `--prewarm 1000` 2) pin kernel selector to previous v0.9 for comparison 3) capture perf profile (nvprof / per-step timeline).

sara: I'll queue both runs. Also adding a short perf-profiling snippet to CI job so we get a flamegraph upload on failures.

ci-bot: queued: replay-runner RERUN (prewarm=1000) and synth-headtohead RERUN (kernel=v0.9) — jobs: #7286 #7287

omar: thanks. Also adding a quick config diff to the nightly job so we don't regress silently. Patch suggestion:

```yaml
jobs:
  nightly-perf:
    matrix:
      - workload: replay
        prewarm: 1000
      - workload: synth
        prewarm: 1000
    thresholds:
      p95_ms: 120
      delta_pct: 15
    profile_on_fail: true
```

rachael: we should be careful—thresholds per-seq-length not global. For seq=1024 p95=120 is fine but for shorter it's too loose. suggest thresholds keyed by shape.

omar: noted. will update to shape-specific thresholds. Also, add KV hit-rate as a metric to alert on (if hit-rate delta > 15% between runs, mark flaky).

matt: question: do we want CI to auto-mute alerts when test is flaky? We already have too many transient failures from replay variability.

jess: don't auto-mute without owner. For flaky alerts, add a triage label and route to eng-runtime oncall. Maybe add a cooldown window: only alert if regression persists for 3 consecutive nightly runs.

sara: added dashboard tile in Grafana: nightly/compare -> p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, kernel_selected. I'll publish after runs complete.

infra-bot: job #7286 completed: replay-runner RERUN (prewarm=1000) — p95=103ms, kv_hit_rate=85%

ci-bot: job #7287 completed: synth-headtohead RERUN (kernel=v0.9) — p95=101ms, kv_hit_rate=87%

omar: looks like most of the regression was warmup-related. Kernel selector still had slight variance (1-2% p95) but within noise.

matt: cool. next steps: 1) revert accidental `--prewarm 0` change in replay-runner config 2) add shape-keyed thresholds 3) add a perf profile artifact upload and small flamegraph parsing step to CI.

rachael: I'll open the config PR and include the threshold per-shape table.

jess: and I'll follow up with a short runbook for triaging perf regressions (what to check: prewarm, kv_hit_rate, kernel selection logs, flamegraph).

omar: perfect. thanks everyone. I'll close the CI alert once PR is merged and we get 3 clean nightlies. :thumbsup:

sara: filing a short postmortem note in #postmortems with links to runs and dashboard.

omar: tagging @sre oncall for visibility.

ci-bot: alert resolved (regression transient due to missing prewarm).
